generating color distributions by counting color frequencies in images is impractical and challenging to verify. Thus, in line with our focus on human perception of color as it relates to language (i.e., color terms), we approximate color distributions via human annotation crowdsourced on Amazon Mechanical Turk (MTurk).
guideline: Workers are shown words representing objects and tasked with rating -on a scale from 1 to 5 - the frequency with which instances of the objects appear in each of the 11 provided colors. We set up these tasks as human intelligence tasks (HITs), and provide the workers with instructions, which include an example for how one could label "grass" and a concrete list of acceptance and rejection criteria.
